title: REST APIs: resources, statelessness, pagination

kcs.statement: REST models data as resources identified by URLs that are nouns (e.g. /users/42/orders) and acts on them with standard HTTP methods instead of verbs in the path.
Each REST request carries everything the server needs (such as an auth token), so the server keeps no per-client session and any server instance can handle any request.
REST list endpoints return results in pages using a limit plus a cursor or offset, so a response stays bounded in size however many items exist.

problem_ideas: Rewrite POST /createTweet, GET /getUserFollowers?id=7 and POST /deleteComment as RESTful endpoints.
Design REST endpoints for a URL shortener: create, redirect, delete, stats.
A feed endpoint returns all 30,000 posts; redesign it with cursor pagination and say why cursor beats offset when posts are inserted.
A server stores the user's cart in its own memory and requests go to random servers; what breaks?
Choose status codes for a successful create, a duplicate username and a missing resource.
Model nested resources for chat: conversations, messages and participants.
